The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

Who Rang the Empty Bell?

Somebody rang the bell by the crooked-roof birdhouse. Ting! Chip hurried to greet his Everybody Day visitor. The path was empty. The bell was still swaying. “You might at least say hello,” he told it.

Ting! This time he peeped behind the post. No visitor. He peeped inside the bell. Nobody in there either. He wrote down his first clue on a paper leaf. He drew a bell.

“Was it you?” he asked Mouse. “I wish,” said Mouse. “I was trying to find your porch from the long grass. That ting is the only part of your house I can find.”

Chip went into the grass with him. Ting! But from down there the sound seemed to come from everywhere. They took three very certain steps toward it and walked into a pumpkin.

Caty stayed by the post to watch. A breeze bent a tall reed. Its seed head brushed the bell. Ting! When the breeze stopped, the reed stood straight and quiet as a whisker.

Chip waved to Mouse. Mouse couldn’t see him. Then Chip rang the bell in pairs. Ting-ting. He waited for Mouse’s little squeak before he rang again. This time Mouse followed the pairs right to him.

“I’d like a turn at welcoming,” Mouse said. Chip held the grass apart and walked back into it. Ting-ting. He answered with a chirp. For once he was delighted to let somebody else know the way.

Chip added a reed beside the bell on his Welcome Tree leaf. The next breeze rang just once. “Good morning, Reed,” said Chip. He could have sworn it bowed.
